notes: Daktronics All Sport 5100 is a tabletop rodeo/motorsports timing and scoring control console (part of the All Sport 5000 Series), not a typical AV signal-routing device - it has no HDMI/SDI/USB/Ethernet; instead it uses D-sub serial ports and current-loop/relay signaling to drive fixed-digit scoreboards and accept photocell/transponder timing inputs. Dimensions 4.25"H x 16.25"W x 9"D, weight 7-7.5 lb, desktop unit (no rackUnits). Two official manufacturer spec sheets were found and used to corroborate dimensions/power: "All Sport 5100 Motorsports Product Specifications" (SL-04357, 2018, https://www.daktronics.com/web-documents/hspr-documents/sl04357.pdf) and "All Sport 5100 Rodeo Timer Product Specifications" (SL050906-04439, https://cdn-docs.av-iq.com/dataSheet/SL04439.pdf) - neither lists rear-panel connector detail. The definitive port list/pinout came from Daktronics' own factory engineering drawing "REAR VIEW, A/S 5100 CONNECTOR ASSIGNMENTS" (Dwg. 1196-R04A-124632, Rev 04), which is bundled into the All Sport 5100 Operation Manual (ED-12501) and was located as a page image on ManualsLib (page 80 of the hosted manual). The connector taxonomy provided for this task has no generic D-sub (DB9/DB15/DB25) or RJ11/RJ12 identifiers, so those physical connectors were approximated to the closest available ids ("rs232" for all D-sub serial ports, "rj45" for the two small modular switch jacks) - see per-port notes for the real connector shape. No SDI/HDMI/USB/network/audio-video grade applies to any port on this device, so "grade" was omitted throughout. Manufacturer part number on the reviewed nameplate is Assy 0A-1196-0002 (5100, 120V) vs 0A-1196-0006 (5120, 230V) - only the 5100 variant's ports were reported here, though J1-J8 are identical between the two SKUs (only mains voltage/plug differs).

ports.name: Scoreboard Output 1 (J1)
ports.note: Current-loop output (Tip=CL+, Ring=CL-, Shaft=GND) to fixed-digit scoreboard; drawn as a phone-style jack, exact diameter not printed on drawing (assumed 1/4" based on Daktronics convention).

ports.name: Main Clock Start/Stop/Horn Switch (J4)
ports.note: Actual connector is a 6-pin modular (RJ12/6P6C-style) jack for switch inputs + relay output; taxonomy has no RJ11/RJ12 option so mapped to closest (rj45, 8P8C) - physically smaller.

ports.name: Computer I/O Port (J5)
ports.note: 9-pin D-sub (DB9) carrying RS-232 TX/RX plus current-loop TX/RX for 'Port 4'.

ports.name: Main Output and Input Port (J6)
ports.note: 25-pin D-sub (DB25) - carries RS-232, RS-485+/-, multiple current-loop outputs/inputs, switch input, relay output, and 10VAC/DC input; taxonomy has no DB25 option so mapped to rs232 as closest single id.

ports.name: Shot/Play Clock Start/Stop/Reset Switch (J7)
ports.note: 6-pin modular (RJ12-style) jack, all pins are switch inputs; same connector caveat as J4.

ports.name: Switch Inputs (J8)
ports.note: 15-pin D-sub (DB15) female - 9 switch inputs, relay common/NO/NC, and a current-loop output; taxonomy has no DB15 option so mapped to rs232 as closest single id.

ports.name: 120V AC Power In (P41)
ports.note: Captive/hardwired AC cord (not a detachable IEC inlet) terminating in a standard US plug. Nameplate on the referenced drawing shows this 'All Sport 5100' SKU as 120VAC/5W; a separate 'All Sport 5120' SKU is 230VAC/5W via its own captive cord (J41). Current Daktronics datasheet (SL-04357, 2018) instead lists a combined 120/240VAC, 6W rating.
